# Working of the Program

#### Course: Learn Python Basics

## Working of the Program

Let's take a closer look at the program you just ran.

In Python, we use the function print() whenever we want to display something on the screen.

The print() function shows whatever is inside it.

For example, this program you ran earlier:

![print() displays the text inside double quotes](data:image/png;base64,)

When you run the code, the output will show the text without the quotation marks.

The quotation marks " " around the text tell Python that this is plain text and should be shown exactly as written.

Without those quotes, Python would get confused, wouldn't recognize the text, and would show an error.
